title: Three-Cheese Pesto Pizza with Fontina and Parmesan
changes_from_base: A thin layer of basil pesto replaces the tomato sauce, and a mix of mozzarella, parmesan and fontina is scattered over in place of plain mozzarella.
summary: Three distinct cheeses with subtly different melting points create a complex, deeply satisfying topping over vibrant basil pesto.

ingredients.item: fine cornmeal or semolina, for dusting
pizza dough, shop-bought or homemade, at room temperature

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Brush 5 ml oil inside a 30 cm pizza tin and dust the surface with 1 tbsp cornmeal or semolina.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Roll and stretch the 340 g dough to fit the tin, making sure to leave a thicker, raised rim around the edge.

steps.title: Spread
steps.text: Distribute 2 tbsp basil pesto evenly across the base.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: In a small bowl, mix together 55 g grated mozzarella, 25 g finely grated parmesan and 25 g grated fontina.

steps.title: Top
steps.text: Scatter the mixed cheese blend over the pesto.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Place the tin on the bottom shelf of the oven and bake for about 20 minutes until the crust is browned underneath and the cheese bubbles and turns just golden.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Remove from the oven and serve at once while the cheese is still soft.

tips: Toss the three cheeses together before topping so they distribute evenly rather than settling in pockets
Bake on the bottom shelf so the base crisps while the cheese on top stays soft and creamy
Shop-bought pesto can contain pine nuts, cashews or other nuts as well as cheese; check the label if cooking for anyone with an allergy.
storage: Keep leftovers chilled and eat within 2 days. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
